speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe the black spots you are seeing in your right eye, and when did this vision loss first begin? Since you have a history of AIDS, have you recently missed any doses of your antiretroviral medications?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of decreased vision and seeing black spots in the right eye. He reports no pain, and the left eye is asymptomatic. He mentions being treated for fungal esophagitis 6 months ago and was diagnosed with Kaposi's sarcoma 2 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of AIDS and recent opportunistic infections, what is your most recent CD4 count and viral load? Are the black spots you see fixed in one spot like a curtain, or do they seem to float around when you move your eye?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Decreased vision and black spots in the right eye. I also have No pain, Left eye is asymptomatic.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your CD4 count is likely low due to your history of Kaposi's sarcoma and fungal esophagitis, I need to check your fundus immediately. REQUEST TEST: Fundoscopy. Do the black spots look like cobwebs or smoke, or do they appear as dark, blurred areas obscuring your central vision?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Fundoscopy shows granular yellow-white opacities around the retinal vessels and multiple areas of dot-blot hemorrhages. CD4 T-lymphocyte count is critically low at 36/mm3. General examination confirms multiple violaceous plaques over the trunk and extremities (consistent with Kaposi's sarcoma) and present cervical lymphadenopathy.

speaker: Doctor
text: The fundoscopy findings of granular yellow-white opacities and hemorrhages, combined with your critically low CD4 count, strongly suggest Cytomegalovirus retinitis. DIAGNOSIS READY: CMV Retinitis.
